metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Finland

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Finland and selected comparisons, based on the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically provides sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each participating country/economy. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable names or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used for variance estimation; therefore, the precise weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. For analysts reproducing these estimates, the recommended approach is to use the official PISA 2022 sampling weights and the corresponding variance estimation method supplied with the database, and to apply the same PV/scaling procedures used by OECD for the creative thinking scale.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because this document is a country factsheet summarizing published PISA 2022 creative thinking scale results (means, proficiency shares, and relative performance) rather than reporting an original student-level predictive model with explicit PV estimation steps. Missing-data handling is not reported in the factsheet because it focuses on descriptive and comparative reporting of OECD-produced estimates, and the detailed imputation/deletion rules are provided in the main PISA technical documentation rather than in this short summary.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Finland results for students who completed the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment as part of the PISA 2022 cycle. It states that, in Finland, 10,239 students in 241 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 59,000 15-year-olds; the creative thinking cognitive test was implemented in 64 countries/economies including Finland, and the factsheet presents the resulting creative thinking proficiency estimates for Finland.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III (Creative Minds, Creative Schools) factsheet summarizes Finland’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Finland’s mean creative thinking score is 36/60, significantly above the OECD average (33), and students’ relative performance is above expectations based on mathematics and reading performance. The factsheet also reports proficiency distributions (83% at least Level 3; 39% at Levels 5–6) and within-Finland gaps by socio-economic quartiles and gender, plus associations between creative thinking and mathematics/reading performance. It further notes COVID-19-related implementation challenges and provides guidance on interpreting estimates for countries/economies with unmet sampling standards.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive OECD PISA factsheet rather than an empirical ML/predictive study. As a result, there is no student-level machine learning model, no explicit training/validation procedure, and no reported PV estimation or missing-data strategy within the provided text. The factsheet reports OECD-produced scale results (means, proficiency levels, and relative performance) and therefore the schema’s ML-specific fields are intentionally left empty.
